_README: The ISL pin the FACTOR-SAMPLER CENTRE pairing is derived against.
WHY A SECOND PIN. tests/fixtures/isl-pinned/PIN.json pins ISL's REQUEST MODELS,
and its pairing answers 'does ISL parse the keys PLoT sends?'. That question is
blind to the one this pairing asks: 'does ISL SAMPLE where PLoT meant?'. The two
need different source files (a sampler lives in src/services, not src/models) and
are re-pinned on different occasions, so sharing one PIN would silently couple a
model re-pin to a behaviour transcript. They are deliberately separate.
WHY THIS SHA. 47f20068 was the sha DEPLOYED to ISL staging when this pairing was
created (2026-08-09). The claim being settled is about deployed behaviour, so the
pin is the deployed sha, not the newest one.
RE-PINNING PROCEDURE (all steps, in order — the standing test fails if any is
skipped, which is the point):
1. Fresh blobless clone of the ISL repo at the new sha, OUTSIDE this repo.
2. Update `isl.sha`, `isl.committed_at`, and EVERY `source_sha256` entry.
3. npx tsx tools/isl-contract/capture-sampler-cases.ts
4. cd <isl-clone> && poetry run python <plot>/tools/isl-contract/replay-factor-sampler.py --isl-repo <isl-clone>
WHY THE HASHES ARE HERE. tests/isl-factor-sampler-centre.contract.test.ts asserts
that the committed transcript was generated against exactly this pin
(transcript.pin_digest == sha256 of the canonical form of this file). Bumping the
pin without re-running the driver turns the suite RED instead of leaving a
behaviour claim silently derived against stale bytes.

isl.pinned_by: Prior-only external factor sampling centre (P0, 2026-08-09). The sha DEPLOYED to ISL staging at the time of measurement. ParameterUncertainty itself is UNCHANGED between this sha and the request-model pin (686fcb7f): `git diff 686fcb7f 47f20068 -- src/models/robustness_v2.py` touches only GoalConstraint.value_frame, so the two pins do not disagree about the class this pairing exercises.

runtime.why_these: FactorSampler needs numpy (SeededRNG wraps np.random.PCG64) and importing robustness_analyzer_v2 pulls src/config, which imports pydantic_settings as a package-init side effect.

source_sha256._note: Every file load-bearing for the SAMPLING claim, plus the import-side-effect files without which the driver cannot even import FactorSampler. The driver verifies each against the clone it is pointed at and REFUSES to run on a mismatch, and it additionally asserts each imported module's resolved __file__ sits inside that clone (an editable .pth can rebind imports to another checkout and every number would then measure the wrong tree).
